data.name: Ribbon_LoadFromAddress
data.value: Load from Address

data.name: Ribbon_LoadFromAddressTip
data.value: Type an address: the site plan (lot, neighbours, buildings, road edges) and the terrain are fetched from Datafordeleren with your own key, imported and loaded, and kept in the model. The project gets real coordinates (ETRS89/UTM32). One Undo. The arrow below: Load Terrain CSV File.

data.name: Ribbon_LoadTerrain
data.value: Load Terrain CSV File

data.name: Ribbon_LoadTerrainTip
data.value: Load a terrain CSV in Jega's own format, as Export writes it. It is checked, kept in the model and framed on the plan.

data.name: Ribbon_Refresh
data.value: Refresh

data.name: Ribbon_RefreshTip
data.value: Puts the site plan back on its coordinates and updates the terrain frame, the terrain line labels, the neighbouring buildings (if shown) and the Toposolid (if made). Runs by itself after Work Direction. One Undo.

data.name: Ribbon_GenerateTerrain
data.value: Generate Terrain

data.name: Ribbon_GenerateTerrainTip
data.value: Generate the Toposolid on the lot: bounded by the lot boundary, shaped by the terrain along it and inside. Replaces the one made before.

data.name: Ribbon_Context
data.value: Context Buildings

data.name: Ribbon_ContextTip
data.value: Show or hide the neighbouring buildings as masses (Generic Models), their heights from Danmarks Højdemodel. Load from Address brings them; if they are missing, they are fetched with your key. Shift+click fetches again. The buildings on the lot too: Settings > Site plan & terrain > Neighbouring buildings.

data.name: Ribbon_LotBoundary
data.value: Draw Lot Boundary

data.name: Ribbon_LotBoundaryTip
data.value: Draw the lot boundary (a filled region of the type "Jega Lot Boundary") exactly on the lot and show the elevations along it. Its corners match the site plan's spot elevations.

data.name: Ribbon_TerrainLine
data.value: Terrain Line

data.name: Ribbon_TerrainLineTip
data.value: Read the terrain along any line you draw: its elevations, and with "Jega Line" the falls, slopes and HIGH / LOW, updated live as you edit the line.

data.name: Ribbon_TerrainLineLong
data.value: In a plan view, draw detail lines along a path, a terrace, a ramp or a drain. Terrain Line starts in "Jega Line (elevations only)": every corner and end gets its terrain elevation and a cross. Switch a line to "Jega Line" in Properties for each piece's fall and slope and the highest and lowest points. Move, stretch or delete a line and the elevations follow at once. Use it to check falls before you design, or to set out elevations for a terrace or a path. Settings > Elevations > Offset adds a height to every elevation (e.g. a paving's thickness).

data.name: Ribbon_Settings
data.value: Settings

data.name: Ribbon_SettingsTip
data.value: Jega's settings. Georeference: real coordinates (ETRS89/UTM32) or manual. Elevations: what Revit's 0 is, the terrain lines. Site plan & terrain: the site plan, the Toposolid and its Terrain level, the neighbouring buildings. Layers: which layers the site plan is drawn with. Data access: your Datafordeler key.

data.name: Ribbon_WorkDirection
data.value: Work Direction

data.name: Ribbon_WorkDirectionTip
data.value: Revit's Rotate Project North: sets Project North as you like. Buildings, site plan and terrain turn together; the coordinates and true north stay. Jega Refreshes after, so the site plan lies straight again.

data.name: Ribbon_ViewNorth
data.value: True / Project North

data.name: Ribbon_ViewNorthTip
data.value: Switches the active plan view's Orientation between True North and Project North, as in Properties. Only in plan views; a view template that sets the orientation keeps it.

data.name: Ribbon_Layers
data.value: Layers

data.name: Ribbon_LayersTip
data.value: Which of the site plan's layers are drawn: Settings, on its Layers tab. At OK the site plan is drawn again with them (nothing is fetched).

data.name: Ribbon_Export
data.value: Export

data.name: Ribbon_ExportTip
data.value: Write the site plan DXF and the terrain CSV from the model to a folder you choose, as they are now: e.g. for a surveyor or the municipality.
